content.title: SpaceX seeks $800B val., theater stocks fall on Netflix news
content.description:
Yahoo Finance Senior Reporter Brooke DiPalma joins Market Domination host Josh Lipton to discuss some of Friday's trending tickers and stories.

Movie theater stocks, like AMC (AMC), iMax (IMAX), and Cinemark (CNK), are moving lower after Netflix's (NFLX) Warner Bros. (WBD) deal was announced.

SpaceX (SPAX.PVT) is reportedly in talks for $800 billion valuation via a share sale, according to the Wall Street Journal.

Southwest Airlines (LUV) lowered its profit guidance for the full year, citing disruption from the government shutdown.

content.title: How Investors Are Responding to the Netflix-Warner Bros. Deal Today
content.summary: Netflix on Friday agreed to buy the movie studio and streaming service of competitor Warner Bros. Discovery. Netflix shares pared their losses Friday morning, while Warner Bros. traded nearly 10% below the acquiring price, reflecting some skepticism on Wall Street.

thumbnail.caption: Aaron M. Sprecher / Getty Images Netflix on Friday agreed to buy the studio and streaming assets of Warner Bros. Discovery.

content.title: Movie Theaters Aren’t Thrilled About Netflix Win
content.summary: Movie theater operators will likely be unhappy with Netflix's $72 billion deal for Warner Bros. Shares of theater exhibitors such as Cinemark and AMC Entertainment, have recently declined on concerns about a Netflix win, Wedbush analysts said in a research note, citing the possibility that Netflix would attempt to significantly shorten the theatrical window or bypass it altogether for most titles.
